title: Built a fully automated crypto trading system. Curious what you think of the results.
author: According-Ad-2638
selftext:
https://i.redd.it/bh2yxkqgnx0i1.png

Hey everyone,

I've been working on an automated crypto trading system for quite a while, covering BTC, ETH, SOL, and XRP.

It's fully autonomous, handling everything from signal generation and position sizing to risk management and execution. No manual trading decisions.

My main focus has always been risk management rather than trying to predict every market move.

I've attached a performance report covering Feb 2025 to Sep 2026, including a comparison with an equal-weight buy-and-hold portfolio of the same four coins.

The trading records come from real trading, not just a backtest. The report also looks at performance using volatility-scaled position sizing.

I'm curious what people here think of the results, especially from a risk management perspective.

I'm also exploring opportunities to move into institutional quant research or systematic trading. My background is in ML research, software development, and trading, though I haven't followed the traditional quant career path.

Would this kind of work be relevant to a prop firm or a quant trading team?

Interested to hear your thoughts.

Both long and short. I focus on BTC, ETH, SOL, and XRP, mainly for their liquidity.

The system handles entries, position sizing, and risk management automatically, evaluating the market tick by tick.

I'd rather keep the exact entry logic private, but happy to discuss the general approach.

comments.author: DatGiantIsopod
comments.body:
They're some pretty tasty results so far.

In general terms - is it a swing trading model? In backtest what max drawdown did you get? Because your Calmar for live trading so far is pretty excellent for crypto.

I have a crypto set-up I'm running small position live now with a similar sort of Calmar in backtest but I'm not really expecting the same for live since some will obvs be due to overfitting. Currently playing around with position sizing and so on. Any general tips you can share for that side of things?

replies.author: According-Ad-2638
replies.body:
Thanks, appreciate it!

It's a fully automated, tick-driven system. Holding periods vary, but average around 5.5 days, so it's closer to swing trading than day trading.

I don't use backtest results to tune the system. The numbers in the report are from live trading, and the drawdown shown is based on closed trades, not mark-to-market.

For position sizing, I'd say start with how much risk you're comfortable taking, not how much profit you're hoping to make. I focus on managing exposure and adjusting position sizes based on market conditions rather than using a fixed size for every trade.

To me, risk management matters more than trying to predict every market move.

replies.author: DatGiantIsopod
replies.body: That’s a helpful way to put it, thanks. When you say you adjust size to market conditions, is that mostly volatility, or more how the account has been doing? And roughly how many positions are you usually holding at once? I’m trying to sanity-check my own sizing against live numbers, so even a ballpark helps.

replies.author: According-Ad-2638
replies.body:
Mostly volatility and risk exposure, rather than just how the account is performing. The system handles position sizing automatically based on market conditions and risk limits.

Looking at my trade records, I usually had around 2–3 positions open at once across BTC, ETH, SOL, and XRP.

Of course, that doesn't tell you the actual capital exposure, but hopefully it gives you a rough idea.

replies.author: DatGiantIsopod
replies.body: Nice one cheers. Do you hold winners until a stop or a time limit, or is there a fixed target?

replies.author: According-Ad-2638
replies.body:
No fixed profit target or holding period.

Before opening a position, the system evaluates the risk and decides how to manage that trade. It also looks at existing positions and potential future trades, so it's managing risk across the whole portfolio, not just one position at a time.

If a position is profitable, it can keep running as long as the risk stays within acceptable limits.

So there's no single exit rule that applies to every trade. The different parts of the system work together, and it handles everything automatically.

comments.author: AoideusWasBanned
comments.body:
About 19 months live is a decent start, but BTC, ETH, SOL and XRP are very correlated, so it's closer to one big crypto bet than four independent ones. I'd regress the daily returns on the equal-weight basket to see how much is just being net long crypto at the right times.

If you pitch it to a prop firm or quant team, they'll probably ask for trade count and the results split by long vs short and by coin first. If one side or one coin carries most of it, better you find that before they do.

replies.author: According-Ad-2638
replies.body:
Good points, thanks for the advice.

Yeah, the four coins are pretty correlated. But I also chose them to spread execution across different order books, not just for diversification. That matters more as capital grows.

The system manages overall exposure and risk across all four, so I don't treat them as independent bets.

And you're right about breaking down the results by long/short and by coin. Definitely worth looking at, especially if I'm presenting this to a prop firm or quant team. Appreciate the input!

comments.author: Ok_Map5721
comments.body:
Nice-looking report, but a few things would change how I read it, especially from the risk side you asked about:

1. The two curves aren't measured the same way. The system is closed-trade equity, buy-and-hold is daily marked prices. Closed-trade equity hides drawdowns inside open positions, so -12.9% vs -64.1% isn't a like-for-like comparison. Mark the system's open positions daily too and see what the max drawdown becomes.

2. Was the volatility-scaled sizing what actually traded live, or applied afterwards to the live trade list? If it's the second, that part is a backtest on top of live trades, and any sizing parameter chosen after seeing the results counts as a tried variant.

3. The benchmark is an easy one in a falling market. A fairer one is buy-and-hold scaled to the system's average exposure. If the system was in cash a lot of the time, most of the gap vs -23.7% is just being out of the market.

4. 283 trades over \~19 months is short for a Sharpe. The standard error on a Sharpe over 1.6 years is around 0.8, so 1.65 is roughly "somewhere between 0 and 3". The curve also looks like most of the gain comes from a few jumps. It's worth checking how much is left without the best 2-3 months.

On the career question: the result alone won't carry much weight with a quant team, but showing the process would. Live fills vs backtest, how many variants you tried, an exposure-matched benchmark, and the answers to the points above. That's exactly the thinking they hire for.

replies.author: According-Ad-2638
replies.body:
Good points, really appreciate the detailed feedback.

1. You're right about drawdown. The -12.9% is closed-trade DD, not mark-to-market. I have the trade records, so reconstructing daily equity using historical prices is something I can work on.

2. The volatility-scaled sizing was used in live trading, not applied afterwards. The system has been running with real capital without any changes since February 2025.

3. Fair point on the benchmark. Managing exposure is a big part of the system, but I agree an exposure-matched comparison would be more meaningful. I haven't calculated the average capital exposure yet.

4. I checked the best-month concentration. Removing the top 2 months still leaves +31.43%, and removing the top 3 leaves +16.60%, compounded over the remaining months. I also never tune the system using backtest results. My research approach uses background knowledge and semi-supervised learning instead.

And thanks for the career advice. My background is in ML research and building live trading systems, but I'm still new to institutional quant. That's exactly why I'm looking to join a team where I can contribute and keep learning.

Really appreciate you taking the time to look into this!
